stories.headline: Criminals detained in hospital set to lose benefits
stories.claim: UK government lays regulations to stop benefits paid to serious offenders detained in hospital.
stories.summary: The government is laying regulations in Parliament to end so-called double provision, which stops offenders detained in NHS psychiatric hospitals from receiving universal credit. The change would affect about 2,500 offenders already in hospital and around 200 a year in future, with the government estimating savings of tens of millions of pounds a year. Victims' families, including the parents of Barnaby Webber and Grace O'Malley Kumar, welcomed the move, while the Conservatives argued Labour had been slow. The regulations are expected to take effect early next year, subject to parliamentary approval, and full financial impacts will be published in the 28 October Budget.

OpenAI found the device on 30 September, filmed Alfozan on 5 October, and the FBI arrested him on 9 October. Prosecutors told a San Francisco court that he had considerable support from the Saudi government and was in frequent contact with a member of the royal family. A federal judge denied him bail on Monday, finding a significant risk he would not appear for trial. If convicted he faces up to five years in prison and a $250,000 fine. The Saudi government did not immediately comment.

stories.headline: Japan launches mission to bring home a piece of the Martian moon Phobos
stories.claim: Japan launched its MMX mission to Mars and its moon Phobos, aiming to return samples to Earth in 2031.

It plans to land on Phobos up to twice in 2029, collect at least 10 grams of material, and send a return capsule to South Australia in 2031. The mission carries contributions from NASA, France and Germany, and US researchers will receive 15 percent of the samples. Officials describe it as the first sample return from the Martian moons.

Prime Minister Mark Carney called it one of the worst peacetime tragedies for Canada's forces.

stories.headline: Google Gemini 4 agents just beat Minecraft with no human intervention
stories.claim: Four Gemini 4 agents completed Minecraft's Ender Dragon fight autonomously, per a Google research paper.
stories.summary: Google researchers report that four Gemini 4 Argon agents completed Minecraft end to end, defeating the Ender Dragon without human intervention. The agents were placed in a randomised survival world using the open-source Mineflayer library, with no assigned roles or game-specific tools, and coordinated through in-game chat and shared memory. They divided tasks, shared warnings and recovered items from dead teammates. The run took 27.23 hours, with 2,783 programs written, 229 messages exchanged and 605 deaths. A fifth agent acted as an observer to check for cheating. The team estimated the cost at $810 at list price, or $1,620 at standard price, and described it as the first fully autonomous completion of Minecraft by AI agents.

stories.headline: Cop17 at a glance: everything you need to know about the UN’s nature summit
stories.claim: UN biodiversity summit Cop17 opens in Yerevan to assess progress on 2030 nature targets, which are largely off track.
stories.summary: The UN Convention on Biological Diversity's Cop17 summit takes place in Yerevan, Armenia, from 19 to 30 October, where governments will assess progress on the 23 targets agreed in Montreal in 2022. Countries have acknowledged they are off track on every target, though 27.5% of land is close to the 30% protection goal. Progress on reforming $500bn of environmentally damaging subsidies is almost nil, and the Cali Fund for private contributions has received only $10,656 in commitments. Funding cuts by the US and European countries add to the challenge, and negotiators face a crowded agenda after the previous Cop16 ended in disarray.

stories.headline: Deepfakes, bots and distrust: How AI is shaping Israel's election
stories.claim: AI-generated content is widespread in Israel's election campaign ahead of the 27 October vote, with Likud the largest user.
stories.summary: DW reports that AI is playing a major role in Israel's election campaign, which votes on 27 October. Researchers at the Open University's Ze Be AI project found that over 14% of more than 44,000 politician posts across Facebook, Instagram, X and TikTok used AI in some way. Likud posted more than 1,800 AI-containing items, around a quarter of its analysed material. Examples include deepfakes of rival Gadi Eisenkot and AI-generated videos from several ministers and opposition leaders. The Central Elections Committee requires AI content to be labelled, but experts say there are few other limits. AI robocalls and AI-driven voting advice are also being used.
key_points: Ze Be AI found over 14% of 44,000+ politician posts used AI in some way.
Likud posted over 1,800 AI-containing items, about a quarter of its analysed social media material.

The round values the company at $300 million, triple its valuation of 18 months ago, and brings total capital raised to over $120 million. stories.claim: Companies are trimming AI spending, with Microsoft and Meta reportedly cutting third-party AI tool costs and Ramp data showing slowing growth.

Microsoft reportedly cut internal spending on Anthropic's Claude by more than a third from a projected annual bill above $1 billion, while Meta reportedly halved its Claude Code users from about 60,000 to 30,000. The Ramp AI Index, published 14 October, showed AI adoption reached 55.9% in September but growth in new customers slowed. Spending per employee among the top 1% of AI spenders fell about 3.1% from its July peak. Separately, a Financial Times report found at least 47 AI infrastructure projects hit setbacks in 2026, and Microsoft withdrew from a data-centre project in Essex over electricity supply concerns. stories.headline: Microsoft set for further crackdown from UK competition watchdog over alleged dominance of the business software scene
stories.claim: UK regulator CMA proposes Strategic Market Status designation for Microsoft in business software.
stories.summary: The UK Competition and Markets Authority is proposing to designate Microsoft with Strategic Market Status in business software. The move follows an investigation into five areas of digital activity, including operating systems, productivity software, security and databases. The CMA says customers find it hard to switch away from Microsoft's ecosystem, which around 20 million UK users rely on each month. stories.headline: Inside the quest to combat Arctic fires and save the planet’s frozen carbon
stories.claim: Researchers are studying ways to fight Arctic wildfires to protect permafrost carbon; a North Fire initiative is launched.
stories.summary: MIT Technology Review reports on the growing effort to address Arctic and boreal wildfires, which are thawing permafrost and releasing stored carbon. Woodwell Climate Research Center, the University of Victoria's Polis Institute and the nonprofit Alaska Venture Fund are partnering on a multimillion-dollar initiative called North Fire. Researchers are weighing options such as controlled burns and rapid fire detection. The article notes that the approach is controversial and that its effect on emissions is still unclear. Boreal fire emissions have nearly tripled since 2001 according to the article.
key_points: Woodwell, the University of Victoria's Polis Institute and Alaska Venture Fund are partnering on the North Fire initiative.
The initiative is multimillion-dollar and aims to study the benefits of fire interventions.
Options include controlled burns, early detection, and in some cases firefighting to protect carbon stores.
Boreal forest fire emissions have nearly tripled since 2001, while global forest fire emissions rose about 60 per cent.
The approach is controversial and its effect on emissions is not yet clear.

stories.headline: Bill Gates warned everyone that AI could cause a billion deaths — this cybersecurity expert explains how realistic that scenario really is
stories.claim: A cybersecurity expert assesses how realistic Bill Gates' warning of AI causing a billion deaths is.
stories.summary: Tom's Guide interviewed David Linthicum, a cloud, AI and cybersecurity consultant, about Bill Gates' warning that AI could cause a billion deaths. Linthicum argues that a superintelligent AI wiping out humanity remains largely hypothetical, since it would need control over critical infrastructure, weapons and biological systems without human intervention. He says the more immediate risks are fraud, deepfakes, data leakage and poorly engineered AI connected to business and government systems. He recommends least-privilege access, human approval for high-risk actions, monitoring and basic defences such as multifactor authentication. He also judges that AI-enabled biological weapons are speculative given the practical barriers.
key_points: The article gathers an expert view on Bill Gates' warning that AI could cause a billion deaths.
Linthicum says a superintelligent AI causing mass harm is technically possible in theory but unlikely today.
The more real risks include fraud, deepfakes, data leakage and poorly configured AI systems.
He recommends least-privilege permissions, human approval for risky actions, monitoring and rollback.
He considers AI-enabled biological weapons speculative because wet-lab barriers remain high.

stories.summary: Albertans are going to the polls on Monday to decide whether the province should remain in Canada or hold a second binding independence referendum. Premier Danielle Smith called the referendum despite arguing it was unnecessary and did not campaign for independence, citing an estimated C$400bn transition cost. stories.headline: Tap water no longer drinkable in Norwegian town as climate-related thawing releases heavy metals
stories.claim: Residents of Longyearbyen, Svalbard, told not to drink tap water due to heavy metal contamination linked to thawing permafrost.
stories.summary: Residents of Longyearbyen in Svalbard, Norway, have been told not to drink tap water because of heavy metal contamination in their main supply, a lake called Isdammen. Scientists link the problem to thawing permafrost exposing pyrite-rich bedrock, which releases metals when it oxidises. Manganese levels were found to be 25 times the recommended limit last September, and sulphate and nickel now also exceed limits, so the ban remains. The mayor says a new water mains supply may be needed, with filtration or desalination options that would be costly and technically hard. Researchers warn similar problems could affect other Arctic communities.
key_points: Longyearbyen's drinking water comes from Isdammen, a dammed lake, and residents have been told not to drink tap water.
Thawing permafrost has exposed bedrock containing pyrite, which produces acid that leaches heavy metals into the water.
Manganese levels were 25 times the recommended limit when first detected last September; they have since dropped.
Sulphate and nickel levels have recently exceeded limits, so the drinking ban remains in place.
Options under consideration include filtration of Isdammen or a backup desalination plant, both described as very expensive.
Scientists warn that similar conditions in northern Canada and Alaska could pose risks to other Arctic communities.

stories.headline: Anthropic is pitching Congress its own AI safety bill, report says
stories.claim: Anthropic is privately lobbying US lawmakers with a draft federal AI safety bill, according to POLITICO.
stories.summary: POLITICO reported that Anthropic has been privately pitching lawmakers a confidential draft bill to regulate frontier AI safety and security, citing three people familiar with the effort. An Anthropic spokesperson said the bill reflects the company's Advanced AI Framework, which it has promoted since June. The draft would allow federal officials to halt a model only where it poses a foreseeable, imminent risk of over $1 billion in damages or of killing or seriously injuring more than 50 people, from a bioweapon, a loss of control, or a cyberattack. It would also create outside evaluators, make Commerce the only agency able to seek a halt, and override some state laws. The move comes amid several competing congressional efforts and a debate about AI companies helping to write their own rules.

The figure sits at the bottom of Beijing's 4.5%-5% annual growth target. Exports, boosted by global demand for AI-related chips and components, have offset weak domestic spending. Property investment fell by more than 20% in the first nine months of the year. Analysts say the growth gives policymakers room to act, and Beijing has recently announced support measures including lower rates for some businesses and subsidies for property buyers.
key_points: Chinese GDP rose 4.5% in the third quarter, up from the previous period but down from 5% in the first quarter.
The result is at the bottom end of the 4.5%-5% annual growth target.

Property investment fell more than 20% in the first nine months of the year.
China's trade surplus is on track to exceed the record $1.2tn seen last year.
Beijing unveiled support measures in September, but economists say their effects are not yet visible; trade tensions with the US and EU remain a risk.
stories.market_take: Weak domestic demand and trade tensions keep pressure on Chinese assets, while AI-linked exporters may benefit.

stories.headline: Electricity costs put UK steelmakers in worst position in three years against EU rivals
stories.claim: UK steelmakers' electricity price premium over France has risen to almost £30/MWh, its highest in three years, per UK Steel.
stories.summary: A lobby group analysis by UK Steel finds British steelmakers' electricity cost premium over French rivals has risen to almost £30 per megawatt hour, the highest level in three years. The group links the widening gap to a surge in global gas prices after the US-Israeli war on Iran and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, since UK power prices are set by gas even when cheaper renewables generate. The gap with France had narrowed to £18/MWh last year, and the gap with Germany fell slightly to about £12 this year. UK Steel director general Peter Brennan argues that direct subsidies are the only realistic fix and has proposed a price cap estimated to cost about £51m a year. The government says it is cutting bills for manufacturers and electricity-intensive firms, and has announced jobs plans for young people in key growth sectors.

Baluch militants have claimed hit-and-run attacks, roadside bombs and shootings targeting the IRGC, Basij and police, including incidents in Mehrestan, Zahedan and Taftan. Analysts say separatist and Islamist groups are coordinating more closely, with four Baluch groups forming the Mobarizoun Popular Front in December 2025. The unrest comes while Iran is at war with the United States and Israel, and Tehran accuses both of backing the militants, which Washington and Tel Aviv have not confirmed in this report. The problem stems from untrusted checksum metadata altering packet headers after validation. The article warns that attackers may now study the flaw, so patching is important for Linux users and cloud operators.

The team also discusses disaggregation in AI infrastructure, comparing it with SK Hynix's proposed processing-in-SSD design.

stories.headline: Pink’s Primetime Turn at the Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show
stories.claim: Victoria's Secret's Pink brand is back in focus, with a Q2 growth rebound and new bra launch under president Ali Dillon.
stories.summary: Victoria's Secret's Pink brand is returning to the spotlight, with the sub-brand taking over the halftime slot at the Victoria's Secret fashion show, livestreamed on YouTube. Brand president Ali Dillon says Pink has refocused on 18 to 24-year-olds and reported high-single-digit comparable sales growth in Q2, its fifth consecutive quarter of growth. The brand launched its Marshmallow bra collection, its first new bra in three years, and opened a SoHo store in May. Pink holds around 20 percent of North American intimate apparel and sells through about 700 stores. Dillon says the brand is also trying to rebuild its apparel business, which is just over half intimates.
